memory_update.text: KALU should remain in the underfollowed lane for domestic-content aerospace aluminum because it is a mid-cap specialty aluminum supplier with explicit aerospace/defense exposure and policy-sensitive risk factors including tariffs, reshoring, sanctions/export controls, and customer regulatory disruptions.

DCO should remain in the underfollowed lane as a niche aerospace/defense engineered-products and subassembly supplier; survival to later layers requires facility-level AS9100/NADCAP evidence, prime-program exposure, and raw-material domestic-content verification.

CRS and ATI are stronger as reference/context anchors for titanium, nickel, superalloy and specialty-material bottlenecks than as underfollowed alpha names because both are now large-cap stocks, but their direct material exposure is high.

Need a focused pass on U.S.-listed sub-$5B forging, casting, fastener, precision-machining, aerospace bearings, specialty coating, heat-treatment and testing/certification companies with disclosed GE Aerospace, RTX, Boeing, Lockheed, Safran or military-engine exposure.

The strongest missing evidence is not broad aerospace exposure but proof of compliant U.S./allied sourcing, customer qualification status, quality/on-time delivery records, AS9100/NADCAP certifications, and available capacity during supplier requalification windows.

summary: Expanded the universe around domestic-content aerospace and defense components with a bias toward second-order suppliers rather than primes. The strongest underfollowed fit is Kaiser Aluminum because it is a mid-cap, U.S.-listed specialty aluminum supplier with explicit aerospace/defense exposure and sensitivity to tariffs, reshoring, and customer supply-chain disruptions. Ducommun fits as a niche engineered aerostructures/electronics supplier to aerospace and defense programs, but its domestic-content/raw-material leverage needs verification. ATI and Carpenter are larger-cap reference/context names because their exposure to aerospace titanium, nickel, superalloys, and specialty materials is direct and unusually pure, but they may already be better recognized by the market. The key research gap is whether these suppliers have verifiable U.S./allied sourcing, AS9100/NADCAP qualification depth, prime customer exposure, and capacity available when OEMs or primes requalify away from foreign-dependent titanium/aluminum sources.
